module_title: British Policies - Commercialization of Agriculture, De-industrialization, and Administration
introduction: At this level, we explore how the British forced the commercialization of Indian agriculture, destroyed traditional handicrafts through de-industrialization, and established modern police and judicial systems to consolidate their control.

core_concepts.title: Commercialization of Agriculture
core_concepts.description: The British forced Indian farmers to grow cash crops (like indigo, cotton, opium, tea, and jute) instead of food grains to supply raw materials to British industries. This led to severe food shortages and frequent famines.

core_concepts.title: De-industrialization
core_concepts.description: Following the Industrial Revolution in Britain, cheap machine-made textiles flooded Indian markets. Meanwhile, heavy import duties were imposed on Indian goods entering Britain. This completely ruined India's world-famous handloom and handicraft industries.

core_concepts.title: Civil Services and Police System
core_concepts.description: Lord Cornwallis replaced corrupt company officials with a regularized 'Civil Service'. He also modernized the police system by appointing a 'Daroga' (Police Chief) in every district.

core_concepts.title: Development of the Judiciary
core_concepts.description: Warren Hastings established Diwani (civil) and Faujdari (criminal) courts in every district. Later, the 'Cornwallis Code' (1793) established the principle of separation of powers (separating revenue administration from judicial functions).

important_entities.name: Karl Marx
important_entities.significance: Commented on British de-industrialization, noting: 'The British intruder broke the Indian handloom and destroyed the spinning wheel'.

important_entities.name: Lord William Bentinck
important_entities.significance: Allowed the use of vernacular languages in courts instead of Persian and introduced the Charter Act of 1833, which theoretically ended discrimination in government employment.

important_entities.name: Lord Macaulay
important_entities.key_fact: Chairman of the First Law Commission
important_entities.significance: He drafted the Indian Penal Code (IPC), laying the foundation for a uniform legal system in India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While Cornwallis is the father of Civil Services and the Police system, the foundation of the modern 'Judicial System' in India was actually laid by Warren Hastings.
Commercialization of agriculture did not benefit Indian peasants. The profits were entirely siphoned off by British merchants, money lenders, and middlemen, pushing farmers into deep debt.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Civil Services, Code (Cornwallis Code), Cornwallis Settlement (Permanent Settlement)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A quick trick to remember the three most significant administrative reforms introduced by Lord Cornwallis.

exam_strategy_tips: Questions asking you to 'Match the Following' regarding Diwani Adalat (Civil cases) and Faujdari Adalat (Criminal cases) are very common.
Remember that the concept of 'Open Competition' for Civil Services was introduced by the Charter Act of 1853.
